Replace row two by row one. The cofactors used in expansion along row two are un-

modified matrix has two equal rows and hence determinant zero.

question.text:
T
For a fixed real n × n matrix A and column vectors u, v, consider D(t) = det(A + tuv ). Which
statement always holds?
(A) D is constant.
(B) D has degree exactly one.
(C) D is of the form a + bt, possibly identically zero.
(D) D has degree exactly n.
(E) D contains only even powers of t.

solution.text:
T
Each updated row is its old row plus a scalar multiple of the same row v . Multilinearity
expands the determinant into terms. Any term using updates from two or more rows has
proportional rows and vanishes. Only the constant and linear terms remain; either or both
coefficients can be zero.

solution.text:
Expansion along the first row gives x(b − d) − y(a − c) + ad − bc = 0. If the points differ,
the coefficients of x, y are not both zero, and the equation defines their line. If the points
coincide, every coefficient vanishes and every point satisfies the equation.
